Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings  
• Sudden painless inability to move left arm on awakening (≈1 h prior).  
• Concurrent left facial tingling, mild dysarthria, mild dysphagia.  
• Vascular risk factors: type 2 diabetes, hypertension, former smoker, moderate alcohol.  

Working diagnosis  
• Suspected acute ischemic stroke (high likelihood) – consistent with abrupt focal neurological deficits and vascular risk profile.  

Differentials supported by DDx  
• Intracerebral hemorrhage – medium likelihood; cannot be excluded without imaging.  
• Transient ischemic attack – medium likelihood, though deficits persisting and worsening.  

Management  
• Emergency referral: Ambulance arranged to nearest hospital emergency department for stroke team evaluation and potential reperfusion therapy.  
• Instructions: Patient advised to unlock door, sit in hallway; clinician remained on line until ambulance arrival.  
• Hospital to perform neuro-imaging, labs, ECG, and stroke pathway assessment.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

1. Acute ischemic stroke – High likelihood: Classic sudden unilateral arm paralysis with facial sensory change and speech/swallow difficulty in patient with HTN and DM.  
2. Intracerebral hemorrhage – Medium likelihood: Same abrupt presentation; hypertension is a risk, but no headache or altered consciousness reported.  
3. Transient ischemic attack – Medium likelihood: Similar initial presentation; less likely as deficits persist and appear to worsen.
